title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
hook: Meta's Llama 3 family, trained on roughly 15 trillion tokens with a 405B-parameter flagship, narrowed the gap to closed frontier models while staying open-weights.
key_points: Models from 8B to 405B parameters, all trained on a significantly larger token budget than Llama 2 per the Chinchilla scaling prescription.
Multimodal extensions (vision, speech, code) built on top of the dense language model backbone.
The 405B model matched or approached GPT-4-class performance on several standard benchmarks.
Continued the open-weights release approach with a custom license allowing broad but not unlimited commercial use.
content_html: Meta's Llama team published the Llama 3 technical paper in July 2024, describing a family of dense transformer models spanning 8B to 405B parameters. The models were trained on a far larger and more carefully curated dataset than Llama 2, with filtering and quality-scoring pipelines applied at scale to produce roughly 15 trillion training tokens.
extra_html:
How it works

Llama 3 uses a standard dense transformer architecture with grouped-query attention for efficiency. Training followed the insight from Chinchilla scaling laws that smaller models benefit significantly from more training tokens; even the 8B model was trained well beyond what earlier norms suggested. Multimodal capabilities were added by training specialized adapters on top of the pretrained language model backbone.

Why it matters

With the 405B model approaching closed-frontier performance on key benchmarks, Llama 3 made the open-weights ecosystem genuinely competitive with the best proprietary offerings at the time, lowering the barrier for research and deployment. Read the full technical paper on arXiv.

related.title: LLaMA: Open & Efficient Foundation Models
related.hook: You don't need a 175B-parameter model to compete. LLaMA trained smaller models on lots of public data — and lit a fire under the open-weights community.

related.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
related.hook: Meta released Llama 2 with open weights and a commercial-use license, giving anyone a strong RLHF-tuned chat model to build on - and kicked off a wave of open-LLM development.

related.title: Chinchilla: Compute-Optimal Scaling
related.hook: Most giant models were starved of data. Chinchilla showed that for a fixed compute budget you should grow parameters and tokens together — and a smaller, longer-trained model won.
